---
title: "Saving a Module on the Board"
unit: 3
cluster: "Using a Display"
---

Code that someone else has written usually comes as a module: a Python file
that we import. MicroPython on the board imports a module from a file saved
in the board's own storage, so before we can use the module, we save its
file there.

In this chapter, we'll learn how to:

- see the files saved on the board
- save a module on the board with Thonny
- import it from the REPL

## The files on the board

The board has a small amount of storage, like a tiny disk. To see the files
in it, connect Thonny to the board and choose **View → Files**. A Files pane
opens with two parts: **This computer** at the top, and **MicroPython device**
at the bottom.

On a new board, the device part shows one file, `boot.py`. MicroPython
created it when it first started, and it runs every time the board starts.
We leave it as it is.

## Saving the LCD driver

The next chapter uses an LCD display. MicroPython has no code for this
display built in, so we use a **driver**: a module that knows how to talk to
the display. The driver we use comes in two files, both from the
[python_lcd](https://github.com/dhylands/python_lcd) project:

- `lcd_api.py`, the commands any such display understands
- `machine_i2c_lcd.py`, which sends those commands to our display

To save the first file on the board:

1. Open <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dhylands/python_lcd/master/lcd/lcd_api.py>
   in the browser. It shows the file as plain text.
2. Select all the text, and copy it.
3. In Thonny, choose **File → New**, and paste the text into the editor.
4. Choose **File → Save as**. Thonny asks where to save it. Click
   **MicroPython device**.
5. Type the name `lcd_api.py`, and click **OK**.

Do the same for the second file, from
<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dhylands/python_lcd/master/lcd/machine_i2c_lcd.py>,
and save it as `machine_i2c_lcd.py`.

The device part of the Files pane now shows three files: `boot.py`,
`lcd_api.py` and `machine_i2c_lcd.py`.

::: {.callout-warning}
The name must be exactly the module's name, followed by `.py`. A file saved
as `lcd-api.py`, or saved on **This computer** instead of the device, gives
no error when we save it. The error comes later, when a program imports the
module.
:::

## Importing the driver

In the REPL, import the class we'll use from the driver:

```session
>>> from machine_i2c_lcd import I2cLcd
```

It prints nothing: MicroPython found the file on the board. Without the file,
the same line gives an error:

```session
>>> from machine_i2c_lcd import I2cLcd
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
ImportError: no module named 'machine_i2c_lcd'
```

`machine_i2c_lcd.py` imports `lcd_api` itself, on its fourth line. So if
only `lcd_api.py` is missing, the error names `lcd_api` instead. Both files
have to be on the board.

## Summary

MicroPython imports a module from a file saved on the board, so a module
that is not built in has to be saved there first.

| Step or code | What it does |
|--------------|--------------|
| **View → Files** | shows the files on the computer and on the board |
| **File → Save as**, then **MicroPython device** | saves the file in the editor on the board |
| `boot.py` | runs every time the board starts; created by MicroPython |
| File name | must be the module's name followed by `.py`, such as `lcd_api.py` |
| `from module_name import name` | imports from `module_name.py` saved on the board |
| `ImportError: no module named '...'` | the file for that module is not on the board, or has a different name |
